definitions.explanation: the temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid

examples.japanese: ⟦{氷|こおり}→氷：02753_koori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{融解点|ゆうかいてん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{零度|れいど}→零度：27531_reido⟧だ。
examples.english: The melting point of ice is zero degrees.

examples.japanese: {金|きん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{融解点|ゆうかいてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{非常|ひじょう}→非常：01598_hijou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧。
examples.english: Gold has a very high melting point.

examples.japanese: ⟦{物質|ぶっしつ}→物質：03608_busshitsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{融解点|ゆうかいてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{調|しら}べる→調べる：01213_shiraberu⟧ことで、⟦その→その：00993_sono⟧⟦{純度|じゅんど}→純度：18774_jundo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{確認|かくにん}する→確認する：25332_kakuninsuru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できる→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: By examining a substance's melting point, you can verify its purity.

notes:
Composed of ⟦{融解|ゆうかい}→融解：08404_yuukai⟧ (melting; dissolution) + ⟦{点|てん}→点：01553_ten⟧ (point). The melting point and ⟦{凝固点|ぎょうこてん}→凝固点：26289_gyoukoten⟧ (freezing point) are the same temperature for a given substance — the difference is the direction of the phase change. In everyday Japanese, ⟦{融点|ゆうてん}→融点：21505_yuuten⟧ is more commonly used as the short form.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {融解点|ゆうかいてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧: to have a high melting point
- {融解点|ゆうかいてん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{低|ひく}い→低い：02947_hikui⟧: to have a low melting point
- {融解点|ゆうかいてん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{達|たっ}する→達する：02129_tassuru⟧: to reach the melting point
- {融解点|ゆうかいてん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{測定|そくてい}→測定：04398_sokutei⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to measure the melting point

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{融点|ゆうてん}→融点：21505_yuuten⟧: melting point — the shorter, more common synonym
- ⟦{凝固点|ぎょうこてん}→凝固点：26289_gyoukoten⟧: freezing point — the temperature at which a liquid solidifies (same temperature, opposite direction)
- ⟦{沸点|ふってん}→沸点：25307_futten⟧: boiling point — the temperature at which a liquid becomes gas
